desc:
The western plains slowly descend until lining the Anduin with a narrow strip of
white sand. On the other side of the river, barely visible from here, the flat
ground stretches out all the way to the horizon, covered in lush green
grasslands. Only a few lonely hillocks, no more than a few feet high, rise out
of the seemingly endless plains there.
name: Grasslands by the Anduin

desc:
The northern plateau comes to an abrupt stop here, with a vertical cliff-face
dropping some twenty feet to a roaring chute below. The air is misty from
droplets of water thrown all the way up here by the flow of water hitting
boulders and canyon walls with abominable force. North-east, a battered stony
ridge can be seen running through the land, splitting it into a higher barren
plateau and lower sloping grasslands.
name: A Rocky Ledge

desc:
The barren image of northern grasslands changes is it is slightly enlivened by a
stream flowing south of here. Several bushes dot the landscape, and even the
grass is a lot taller and greener than those that can be seen farther away. To
the east, the stream has cut a gorge into a ridge running through the
grasslands, a few miles away from here.
name: Plains by the Stream

desc:
The stream continues to travel calmly along the plains of the surrounding
landscape. The water appears to get slightly deeper and an increase of the fish
inhabitants is more noticeable near the centre of the stream. Plains can be seen
to the east and west of you which seem very fertile given off by the presence of
the lively green grasslands.
name: Stream through the Plains

desc:
The stream seems to get slightly larger as it travels southward heading into
what one would predict to be a greater mass of water. The calmness of the stream
allows one to easily navigate back and forth through the waters and onto the
stream's shores. In the distance to the north lies many great plains in the
endless landscape. Small fish can be seen trying to swim along with the small
current of the stream water.
name: Stream through the Plains

desc:
The terrain here can be seen quickly ascending as it begins to stretch towards
the stream nearby. A few yards away, it levels off into a small terrace that
forms a viewpoint from which anyone could easily make simple observations.
Heading towards the small terrace, you can overlook the stream and glance at the
vast grasslands that encompass the surrounding land. A small crumbling building
can be seen in the distance to the south.
name: Steep Bank Overlooking the Stream

desc:
As the stream continues to flow eastward the pace of the water ever so slightly
speeds up as it bends to the south. As you go further along the small stream the
water level seems to get deeper, contouring to the earth's natural sloping
nature. An old crumbling building can be seen in the far distance to the south,
but gives off the impression of vacancy set by its rotting wooden structure and
its mossy covered walls.
name: Stream Bend in the Plains

desc:
A lonely majestic pine tree dominates the landscape, looking over the sloping
grassland spreading in all directions. West of here, the ground descends steeply
towards the valley, at the bottom of which a shallow but moderately paced stream
is flowing. The sandy ground is covered by many pine-needles and several cones
shed from tall but growing trees.
name: A Rising Ground

desc:
As the ground starts rising steeply eastwards the stream bends to the right,
finding its way to the bottom of the fertile valley. Few pines dot the landscape
and the grass is tall here, unlike up on the plains where it is beaten and bent
by a constant wind. Although the stream is rather narrow, the water is
swift-flowing and fording it can prove more difficult than it might initially
look.
name: A Stream through a Lush Valley

desc:
The ground is rising eastwards, to form a small hillock just about a mile away
from here. The vegetation seems to grow thicker in that direction, but here it
is just an odd bush among the wind-beaten grass. A wide river can be seen
flowing further to the east, with the opposite bank barely more than a line at
the horizon. To the west, a steep incline climbs to a rocky plateau. In all
other directions, sloping plains with a sea of tall grass flowing in the wind
covering them continue as far as an eye can see.
name: Barren Fields

desc:
Thick grass grows up to the waist-level of an average man here, flowing in eerie
waves in the relentless winds. Several unmistakable signs indicate that this
place has been a ground for a fierce battle sometime in the past. Occasional
cracked skulls, both orkish and those of men, bleached white by sun and rains
are lying around, half-hidden among the grass and the carcasses of horses and
wargs. Broken spears and swords alongside battered pieces of armour dot the
ground, slowly being overtaken by fast-growing grass which is well nourished by
the blood that has been shed here.
name: Waist-high Grass Fields

desc:
Several sharp rocks and boulders rise from waist-tall grass here, with low and
wind-bent bushes growing in their shadow, seeking a shelter from the wind.
Southwards, the grass becomes lower, and in a couple of miles, the fields
descend into a wide river, cutting through seemingly endless grass- lands that
continue in every direction. Few rain-polished rib cages of horses, almost
hidden in the tall grass, betoken a distant battle that has been fought here. A
prominent mound of rocks, covered with moss and small bushes, suggests that
someone important has fallen here.
name: Battered Fields

desc:
The large pasture stretches for a few miles along each side with an extensive
and unbroken fence surrounding the pastured land. There is a gate to the north
that opens and allows access out of the barn's fenced pasture. What would seem
to have supported many cows once long ago is now home to only a few inhabiting
cows that remain living throughout the many years of neglect by their previous
owners. The soil still maintains some nutrients enabling some cow life to live
day after day, yet given some time as the years pass by and if continuing at the
same rate, will become lifeless and inanimate.
name: Desolate Cow Pasture

desc:
Following the ground closely, a distinguished path can be recognized leading
into what seems like a rundown old farm house to the east. Even though the size
of the property might appear to be rather large, the inhabitants of this
building have long since left the land to decay naturally. A cow pasture with a
large and extensive fence can be viewed to the south that has restricted the
movement of the remaining cattle, which survived throughout the years that have
passed.
name: Path Leading to a Ruined Farm House

desc:
Walking carefully on the damp terrain you notice your feet half submerged into
the earth. Given the slight slope of the small stream's shore bank, one could
easily slip and fall into the ever so peaceful water flow. Given time and age,
the landscape here could very well become a marshy swampland inhabited by moss
and fungi. The patches of grass beneath your feet are very limp and hung over,
caused by the nearby water source.
name: Damp Plains along a Small Stream

desc:
The hilly ground to the west gives way to sloping plains that seem to be rolling
for miles and miles towards the Anduin in the east. The vegetation is becoming
thinner, and only a few sparse pines remain from the forests further up the
hills. A narrow but fast-flowing stream is coming from the mountains and finds
its way towards the river, zigzagging through the grasslands.
name: A Stream in the Plains

desc:
A small rivulet follows the bottom of the valley and heads away from the rising
slope eastwards, atop of which an old decaying structure can be seen in the
distance. The large structure to the south looks rundown as if not taken care of
for several years. The south bank appears to have been cultivated in the past,
but now it is fast overgrowing with tall grass and young bushes.
name: A Stream in the Plains

desc:
Vegetation grows scarcely on the exposed surface of the plateau. Only stunted
scrub and small, twisted bushes with prickles all over can survive here,
half-hidden among the rocks. The ground is mostly ash-coloured, like the stone
that forms it. Many cracks and chinks run along its surface, although not wide
nor deep enough as to make a real obstacle to your advance. The plateau comes to
a sudden end to the east, as a steep slope leads into the fields below.
name: Barren Plateau

desc:
The plains are slowly rising towards the west, from lush riverside meadows into
higher and bleaker grasslands, exposed to cold winds from the Misty Mountains.
The slope is seemingly growing steeper still further down south, for in a couple
of miles it can be seen breaking into a ridge, separating the wide berth of
Anduin from the first foothills of mountains far away.
name: A Slope to the Plateau

desc:
A ridge, almost fifteen feet high, rises from the sea of waist-high grass. It is
crumbled in places, which makes it possible to ascend to the higher plateau
behind its edge. Boulders, apparently broken lose from the stony wall, lie
scattered around, surrounded by low and wind-bent bushes.
name: A Worn-Out Ridge

desc:
Western slopes begin to level here, with ground slowly descending towards a
majestic wide river, a further few hours' walk away. Although still exposed to
the elements, the landscape isn't quite as barren the closer one gets to the
Anduin. In addition to low bushes, some trees dot the land, and several groves
of trees that appear to be willows can be seen further east and south, lining
this bank of the River Anduin.
name: Grasslands

desc:
A worn-out stony ridge runs through the grasslands, with rubble and broken
boulders crumbling from its steep face, making it possible to climb it with a
little care and some effort. Eastwards, gently sloping grasslands continue for
several miles, and terminate by a wide river.
name: A Crumbling Ridge

desc:
A gravelly film of grey dust slides along the worn surface of the ground, pushed
by a wind that seems to never stop blowing here. Particles of rock, and even
small pebbles, are carried away, swept by the air, until they crush into a
larger stone, or disappear into dark crevices. The sound of the grain grazing
the earth spreads all over the plateau, merging with the howl of the wind.
name: A Barren Plateau

desc:
A high, peculiar crag rises suddenly out of the uniform plateau. The softest
areas of rock have mostly disappeared, devoured by the wind. Other surfaces,
that seem harder, have somewhat withstood the erosion, and they show a better
condition. Thus, the outline looks sharpened and irregular, as if serrated. All
around the pinnacle, rocky fragments of all sizes lie scattered on the flat,
grey ground.
name: A Crag in the Middle of the Plateau

desc:
Small rises, standing a bit further north, partially shelter this area from the
lashing, icy wind. The ground looks rocky and barren, and the landscape rather
featureless, except for a number of little, weak trees, battered by the cold and
elements, that grow scattered around. But even so, only a few blackened, pointed
leaves still stick to their bare, greyish branches.
name: Barren Plateau

desc:
Approaching the edge of the plateau a section of the ground seems to have given
way, and melts into the lowland below. Observing along the split terrain, the
inner rock can be seen exposed to the light giving notice to its faint grey
surface deep within the crevice. The ground around you is absent of living plant
life and is overpowered by the many small boulders and scattered rocks that have
been naturally set by the earth's natural weather conditions.
name: Edge of the Plateau

desc:
Walking towards the slight incline of the nearing plateau, the ground can be
seen opening up its way to the top of an exposed landscape. The only sign of
vegetation is the plant growth hidden behind the many rock formations across the
plateau. Travelling further up the inclined land would give way to a lifeless
earth only inhabited by the inanimate rocks that occupy the land at arm's reach.
name: A Bare Incline to the Plateau

desc:
The land continues to rise creating a sloping ground, which makes walking more
tedious if one were to travel farther east through the landscape. Noticeable
from this distance is the large plateau to the east, which opens widely in the
distance not far ahead. A small stream can be seen heading in a southerly
fashion, but slightly hidden within the valley's edge.
name: Rising Plains entering the Plateau

desc:
The terrain here can be seen ascending northward towards the dry plateau that
lies in the distance. There are noticeable amounts of dotted grass formations
buried on the surface of the many rocks that lie around in the surrounding area.
Some of the rocks probably fell from the rocky wall to the east. The wall is
mostly stone, but there are sections of earth from which vegetation sprouts. A
small stream lies in the distance to the south and can be seen flowing further
into the south.
name: At the Foot of the Plateau

desc:
As bare as the ground may seem, many of the protruding rock formations rising
from the ground beneath you could cause injury if a misplaced step was taken.
The rocky walls of the empty plateau can be seen, plummeting down to the ground
below. In rainy conditions small waterfalls can be seen forming, caused by the
small brooks that slide down the cliff-face. In the nearby landscape, some form
of grass formation can be seen but yet not abundant enough to create a field.
name: Edge of the Barren Plateau

desc:
The plateau comes to an end here, except for a ledge projecting southwards and
westwards. The dry weather and lack of water has caused the ground to harden up
and become extremely manageable to walk on. Overlooking in the westerly
direction, the rock face descends steeply into the sloping terrain. The
occasional cracking of a rock flying off the cliff to hit the ground breaks the
sound of the winds that sometimes howl around this cliff. Further out into the
distance, a large land of grasslands can be seen from above.
name: Corner of the Plateau

desc:
The land is full of lush and lively grasses that the water has helped to grow
for many years now. There are numerous rock formations in the surrounding
landscape which have probably fallen from the nearby plateau over time. The
impressive cliff-like face of the plateau stands majestically to the east, as if
it had been rooted out of the ground. Dew is common in the mornings when the
shadow of the plateau shrouds the land in darkness until the sun is high in the
sky.
name: Steeply-sloping Ground

desc:
A decaying barn obstructs your passage to the west. The only means of passage is
to go around the large fence surrounding the old barn to the south or by
swimming through the nearby stream to the north. The land here is very fertile
and gains its nutrients from the lively stream to the east and north.
name: Fertile Plains

desc:
The stream continues to travel in a southerly direction, bending to the east
overflowing into a larger and slightly faster-paced stream. Small movements can
be seen under the watery surface indicating signs of fish life up ahead.
Continuing to journey along the stream's route will only lead you to greater and
much faster flowing water, which only the most experienced swimmer could
navigate through.
name: A Stream in the Plains

desc:
An old building sits lonely on a flat plain overlooking the river, with its
straw roof fallen in and crumbling chimney pointing to the sky above. Its
decaying walls are slowly being overtaken by grass and vines. The last remaining
doors and window shutters are still somewhat intact but the hinges squeak as the
wind blows through them. The pasture behind the farm still contains what little
life there is. Whoever once lived here must have left a long time ago.
name: Ruins of an Old Farm

desc:
This slowly decaying cow pasture is contained by a large fence and has a broken
down barn door in it. The fence blocks your path in more than one direction,
which constrains your movement. There are only a few cows still left standing
about that have been able to live off the still depleting nutrients that exist
within the soil in the pasture. Given some time this pasture will be as lifeless
and inanimate as the rest of the farm.
name: Desolate Cow Pasture

desc:
There are only small portions of loose grass remaining in the surrounding
landscape. Observing more closely, signs of heavy passage can be seen crossing
the ground beneath you in all directions. All that remains is the permanent
damage done to the flourishing grasslands that once encompassed the land long
ago. There is a large fence preventing your travel to the east and the only
access to get inside that pen would be to walk around to the front entrance
which would take some effort considering the descending hill before the
entrance.
name: Decaying Fields on a Hill

desc:
The landscape here descends down into the vast plains below. Travelling towards
the plains below will only lead to a task that requires some work of a skilled
climber. To the east is a ruined barn with a large wooden fence surrounding it.
A small stream can be seen from the top of this hill and can be followed with
the eye, flowing to the south-eastern direction. Further to the south the hills
become more ridged and harder to travel along the terrain.
name: Decaying Fields on a Low Hill

desc:
A mist of water can be felt coming from the northern direction. The ground
beneath you seems to sink in about half an inch as the spray settles on the
floor and becomes absorbed by the soil, turning into wet earth. Badly decaying
fields of grassland can be seen from the horizon and a sense of warfare can be
felt in the frigid wind blowing around you. Travelling in the south-westerly
direction can only satisfy one's curiosity of the remains left behind of a
battle taken place many years ago.
name: Soggy Plains along a Small Stream

desc:
As the ground drops the rapids become a series of small falls and streams,
throwing mist and vapour into the air as the water finds its way among the
slopes and steps. A few of the falls are several feet high, but by being careful
enough you can probably ford the stream with little or no trouble. Trees are
becoming sparser when you move eastwards, where only vast sloping plains and
grasslands extend as far as your eye can see.
name: Cascades

desc:
Although the stream through these parts is rather small, the water flows
extremely fast. The current is strong enough to easily knock a man off his feet
and carry him downstream. Flowing with determination towards the eastern rim of
the large vale, it's clear to assume these rapids will result in a cascade of
small waterfalls and streams farther away to the east. To the south is a vast
expanse of battle-scarred plains.
name: Small Rapids

desc:
The ravages of war are seldom more evident then they are upon this place. Soil
rich with the blood of fallen warriors has only recently healed enough to allow
new growth. A few weeds have sprouted up through the shallow graves of limbs
lost by those who fell in battle.
name: Fields of Sorrow

desc:
The sound of the wind sweeping across this old field could easily be mistaken
for the howl of a dying man. Everything about this place conjures up the memory
of death. Soil rich from soaking up the bloodshed of a great battle also holds
the broken bones and mangled armour of those bodies left to rot without so much
as being placed in a shallow grave. Since that time a few straggling weeds have
managed to take seed and begin to heal this once fertile land.
name: Fields of Sorrow

desc:
Despite the vast destruction of the surrounding areas, this flat parcel of land
seems to have been for the most part spared. Bushes and even a few groups of
young trees grow upon the sparsely grass-covered ground. However, this place is
not without its scars. While it doesn't appear that armies clashed on this spot,
the footfalls of troops passing by have left some patches of ground notably
bare.
name: Surviving Fields

desc:
In the spring when the sun smiles upon this vast plain this fertile land bursts
with flowers. A hardy variety of plant, the blooms last all through the summer
months. In the fall, when all their petals have dried and fallen to the ground,
this area gives off a sweet smell. In the winter, there is very little growth,
while the bulbs of those flowering plants safely nestled in the soil are waiting
for the cycle to begin again.
name: Dazzling Fields

desc:
The plants here have never recovered from the trampling of armies during what
must have been a great battle. The once blood-stained earth still carries the
broken bones and battered armour of the fallen warriors. In some places the
fletching of an arrow or the hilt of a sword can be seen protruding from the
ground.
name: Fields of Sorrow

desc:
It is hard to imagine this quiet spot was once the site of a great battle. The
soft soil, home to a variety of weeds and grasses, almost obscures the remnants
of bones that lay as silent markers to those who died and were not even buried.
name: Sleeping Meadows

desc:
The stream straightens out here and picks up speed on its journey eastward.
Still quite calm, it emits a pleasant transparent sound as it passes the meadows
that grace its shores. Some small birds flutter about bathing in the water and
drinking from the cool, clear stream. Some other birds along the banks sing
sweet songs, as if to thank the gods for placing this stream upon Arda.
name: Small Rapids

desc:
This small trickling stream winds through the plains. The water is crystal clear
and flows quickly, inviting weary visitors to take a dip. As the stream slowly
wanders back and forth on its way eastward towards the Anduin River it produces
a small tinkling sound. Small animals come and go, stopping only to drink from
the banks of the river.
name: Small Stream

desc:
Almost utterly silent is the meadow that unfolds upon this land; the only sound
to be heard is the whisper of a small stream. The stream speaks with nature's
dulcet voice trying to maintain harmony, lest other less peaceful sounds would
try to overwhelm this quiet place.
name: Sleeping Meadows

desc:
The land gradually slopes to the west. At dusk when the wind blows it creates
the illusion of these winsome grasses bending to pay homage to the setting sun.
This entire area seems to carry an air of simplistic calm. Each morning these
tranquil plains seem to awaken with life.
name: Slanting Plains

desc:
This is one of the few inns in this part of the land; unfortunately there is not
much left of it. A large pile of broken wood scraps lies heaped in the middle of
the floor. There is a staircase at the eastern side of the inn, suggesting that
at some point there used to be a second floor to this building. The staircase
does not lead anywhere now, as the walls have been demolished, with the roof
collapsing in on top due to lack of support.
name: Ruined Inn

desc:
There are rumours of a great chieftain of the woodsmen, who lived in this area.
His exact residence was not certain, but it may have been this village. This old
lodge would most likely have been his dwelling. Not much is left intact, save a
large wooden bookshelf against the northern wall. Next to the eastern wall the
bed has taken heavy damage from an axe and now lies splintered and broken. A
shattered desk has been left heaped at the western wall.
name: Ruined Lodge

desc:
In the middle of a large carpet of shattered limestone stands a large altar made
of white marble, as evidence of the glorious chapel that once stood here. Now
the altar is the only remaining vestige of that chapel, for those things that do
not lie shattered on the ground among the limestone have probably been stolen or
burnt.
name: Ruined Chapel

desc:
Apart from the surrounding ruins this old square has remained completely intact.
A large white fountain containing two remarkable statues at its centre is the
most noticeable of this courtyard's features. One of the statues depicts a huge
bear standing upright. The other one is of a large man, in ranger's dress,
wielding a beautifully carved longbow.
name: An Old Square

desc:
Pieces of shattered and charred rock lie scattered all over the ground, mixed
with piles of debris and burned wood. What was once a house is now a mere pile
of rubble, all former markings and traces of architecture obliterated by some
great force.
name: Ruins of a House

desc:
A small, almost square flat area at the top of the stone provides a perfect
vantage point for observing the surroundings. The path leading down to the foot
of the hill appears very well trodden indeed, and leaves no doubt that this
place has been visited often over the years.
name: Atop the Carrock

desc:
The largest river in Middle-earth advances steadily southbound, to meet the salt
waters of the still very distant Belfalas Bay. Its water, proceeding from the
icy basins of the Grey Mountains, keeps cold to the touch for the whole year.
Its surface is always limpid and clear, like a window through which the Great
Vala Ulmo, Lord of the Sea, watches the land. For even here, many miles inland,
among dense forests and high mountains, it is Ulmo who keeps control of every
little pool and tiny brook.
name: The Meandering Anduin River

desc:
The wide river continues its way towards the sea, running through these vast
grasslands that extend between the snowy peaks of the Hithaeglir and the dark
and sinister Mirkwood forest. The flow avoids every little roughness of the
ground in an endless series of gentle bends. Here, the river runs into a small
hillock, and it turns westwards to detour it. But throughout the years, the
stream has worn away the hillside, and now it towers vertically over the cold
waters.
name: A Meander in the River

desc:
The simple beauty of these lands shows clearly in this riverbank. A gentle,
grass-covered embankment descends softly to the riverside, where the quiet and
silent waters seem to caress the little round stones on the ground as they flow
along. Now and again, a tiny wave comes to the shore, but it fades away before
breaking, as if it dared not making any noise that might disturb the quietness
of this spot.
name: Wet, Grassy Bank

desc:
A small, lonely hill stands to the east, like a lump on the ground that stands
out of the grassy plains around, and it is towards its top that this hillside
rises, gradually but steadily. As it ascends, some weeds and scrubs begin to
show among the grass, as if the latter ruled undisturbed in the low lands but
the other plants challenged its reign on high. To the northwest, at the river-
bank, you can see an old pier floating on the quiet waters of the Anduin.
name: Wild Slope

desc:
The half-rotten but still recognizable remains of an old landing stage float
mildly on the quiet waters of the river, along the eastern bank. Long ago, trade
was intense and prolific in these lands, but the declining of Gondor and the
strengthening of the orkish settlements in the mountains made an end of it. In
those days, small barges sailed the river, light enough to allow portaging when
they reached the Anduin rapids, to the south. But those were better times, and
the fine goods from Gondor are now rarely seen this far north.
name: River by a Ruined Pier

desc:
For a moment, a heavy gloominess seems to engulf the river, as it runs along the
withered western bank, where everything looks wasted and desolated. The waters
seem to darken and turn cloudy and turbid, as if trying to conceal some ominous,
forbidden secret that may lie hidden on the river floor. And they even seem to
hasten, trying to leave this place behind as soon as possible.
name: A Mournful Section of the River

desc:
Slowly but steadily, the waters of the Anduin continue their long travel
southbound, having started many miles away at the icy springs in the Ered
Mithrin, in the northern vales. Here, the stream has flooded the eastern bank,
forming a small marsh where vegetation grows dense. On the contrary, a low
hillock stands on the western riverside, silent and mysterious, and somehow it
seems as if the own mighty Anduin avoided its slope.
name: The Great Anduin

desc:
The river once again stretches out on its way far to the south, the water
flowing slowly but purposefully towards the sea miles away. A cooling breeze
runs over the surface of the river, creating ripples and dancing on the water.
Along the shores can be seen small streams of rainwater adding to the might of
the river in its journey south. To the east the bank rises unto great, rolling
grasslands that stretch out as far as the eye can see. To the west the Misty
Mountains can be seen looming in the distance.
name: The Great River Anduin

desc:
Pouring down over the ledge of black rock, the great river falls a short
distance here. A cold wall of spray rises up from the chute. The seething
current is coursing around everywhere, throwing forward everything and anything
that gets in its way and pulling it back with a relentless force. If careless
enough, one might not break the pull of the river, and end up in the deep and
dark surface of the mighty flow.
name: A Strong Eddy in the River Anduin

desc:
The great river rises here in a swell of foam and spray as it sweeps over the
top of massive black rocks lying just beneath the surface of the water. The
jagged edges of the rocks have been worn down with the eternal flow of the
current, but they still churn the waters and make passage difficult, even for
the experienced boat pilot. A quick glance reveals that the eastern bank of the
river is lined with dark mud, while open grasslands hasten away in the distance.
name: Rocks in the River Anduin

desc:
The waters of the River Anduin seem dark and forbidding and give away no hint of
what lies deep beneath the surface. The river is vast, the large body of water
flowing at a stately pace towards the distant south. Small fish can be seen just
beneath the surface, trying to catch a glimpse of the sunlight. To the far west
the peaks of the Misty Mountains loom, and to the east vast, rolling plains
stretch out.
name: The Mighty River Anduin

desc:
The central channels of the River Anduin sweep by, silent and grey, leaving only
subtle markings on the surface that belie the power of the swift under- current.
Schools of fish can be seen feeding in the warmer currents near the surface,
while the murky depths of the Anduin hide the passage of the larger predators.
White against the distant sky, the lofty peaks of the Hithaeglir rise to the
west, while to the east the rocky shore melts into an endless plain of rolling
grasslands.
name: The Mighty River Anduin

desc:
The grey surface of the water slides by swiftly, a swirling pattern of whirls
and ripples catching and reflecting the light. An occasional branch or bole of
some mighty tree drifts by, soaked and half-submerged in the powerful flow. The
distant shorelines are lined with tall and hoary willows, their grey roots
twisting down the low banks. The western horizon is sharply dominated by the
majestic peaks of the Misty Mountains, while rolling grasslands stretch away
eastwards toward the distant and unseen eaves of Mirkwood.
name: The Mighty River Anduin

desc:
This field of grass and wildflowers lies directly west of the great river
Anduin. The shores are low and sandy, making a perfect place to launch a vessel
into the river, should one attempt to cross. The great river would make any
attempt to wade or ford it impossible because it is just too wide. Looking to
the west, you spy in the distance the great Misty Mountains, while the eastern
banks of the river are lined with stands of willows.
name: A Grassy Riverbank

desc:
Long ago, after a glorious but painful victory against the dark minions, the men
of the northern vales dug out a barrow for their fallen people. The Nenedain, as
the elves call them, chose this small hill near the bank. It was hollowed out of
the very earth, and a huge stone was set to block the way in. Nowadays, the tomb
remains intact. The grass grows green and fresh over the hillock, but, strangely
enough, there is no sign of animal life nearby, as if some unknown power scared
the beasts. Perhaps it is the same power that has protected the place from
plundering.
name: An Old Barrow

desc:
The crudeness of an old battle, waged countless moons ago, has forever set its
indelible mark in what once was a beautiful riverside. The ground is scrambled
and spoiled; dense, black, dried stains fill the bottom of the holes among the
wasted earth, and desolation extends wherever you look. Everything seems still
and quiet, almost frozen, but sometimes the clashing of swords, the screams of
fighting men and the howls of orcs and wargs seem to come back from the past
like a soft, almost inaudible echo, rising from the ground itself.
name: Wasted Riverbank

desc:
A huge, coal-black stain is all that remains of a one-time green and fresh
riverbank. The grass, that once grew high and dense, has been burnt to the root
and blackened ashes have taken its place in the ground. Now and again a slight
glint catches your eye, perhaps some metal that didn't melt down, or maybe the
dried remnants of orkish blood, for this desolation is the result of a huge
pyre. The men of these lands, though kind and hospitable to their kin, hate orcs
and wargs beyond imagination and they are cruel and merciless to their enemies.
name: Burnt Riverside

desc:
A short flight of narrow and dusty steps, crudely carved out of the very ground,
descends into the hillock and opens into this square chamber with a low, rocky
ceiling. A great niche draws your attention to the rear wall, surrounded by a
coarsely-depicted but vivid battle picture. Below it, an inscription has been
engraved on the gravelly stone. Along both side walls many other smaller niches
fill most of the surfaces. The air is extremely dense and heavy inside the
chamber, and stale when you breathe it, as if it had remained still, waiting for
who knows how long.
name: A Chamber Hollowed out of the Earth

desc:
A soft slope rises northwards to where an old, tumbledown-looking building with
walls made out of rough logs and a thatched roof still stands rather
precariously. A bit eastwards, in a small valley between two hills, thin columns
of white smoke climb into the sky from a little village with hardly a dozen
huts. Down the hillside, to the south, a group of ancient trees seem to
withstand the advance of the vast grasslands that extend all around up to the
horizon and beyond.
name: A Wet Hillside

desc:
In this section of the meadow, all kind of flora blooms among the grass stems.
Large and small flowers of many different colours with intense scents abound,
their petals taking every imaginable shape. But there are also other plants:
thick, short, rough stalks, bulbous tubers, leaves sharp as blades or even
thorny plants. They all grow dispersed among the green grassy background, as in
a small vegetal sanctuary, or perhaps a garden for Yavanna's delight.
name: Fertile Plains

desc:
These vibrant meadows are the colour of emeralds, their lush, green grass
covering most of the ground. In the small spots where the grass does not grow,
beautiful flowers of red, blue and yellow grow in abundance. Surprisingly, the
fertile soil has not been cultivated, but to the south one can spot signs of
human hands: rows of beehives stand there. Some bees seem to have found their
way here in their search for new, fresh flowers. In all other directions the
plains stretch out.
name: Meadowlands

desc:
Here stand, in small groups, a variety of different trees. One can spot birches,
beeches and even a few lonely oaks. The grass that grows beneath the trees seems
to be shorter than that covering the plains, but not much else grows in the
shadow of the trees. To the south lie the more fertile vales of the Anduin,
while to the north, east and west the vast plains stretch out.
name: Forested Plains

desc:
These low, flat lands obviously hold better soil than the surrounding area, as
lonely, great beech trees grow here, stretching their branches towards the
distant skies. They look like great beings where they stand, keeping their
distance between themselves. In their shadow, low grass and a variety of flowers
and herbs grow. To the north and east, the great plains roll out, while to the
west the bank of the Anduin rises. To the south the trees stand closer.
name: Sparsely Forested Plains

desc:
This low rise is more exposed to the wind than the lands that lie about it, and
yet a good place for the living. Small trees grow about, casting shadows over
the grass and giving the rise a distinct air in comparison with the
surroundings. To the east the great plains roll out under the sky, while to the
west the great Anduin flows, like a tongue of steel in the green landscape.
name: A Sparsely Forested Rise

desc:
Here the banks of the Anduin resemble a marsh more than anything. In this soft
and moist soil some grey willows have placed their roots. Their long, thin
branches stretch out and hang to the ground, giving the place a sad and almost
ghost-like appearance. To the west lies the great Anduin, while to the east the
land rises unto great, rolling plains.
name: A Marshy Stand of Grey Willows

desc:
The waters of the Great Anduin have swamped the bank here, making use of the
earthy, rockless ground. A small marsh has formed, where vegetation grows thick.
The tall stalks of the reeds sprout out of the flooded ground, like a tiny but
dense forest that sometimes hinders your advance. The marsh seems to spread
southwards, and to the east, there is still vegetation to be seen, although much
more sparse compared to the other areas.
name: Rushy Marsh

desc:
The tall and strong stems of the reeds sprout out of the pools that cover the
ground everywhere. At times, they form little clusters, at other times they grow
in dense groups. The ground beneath your feet is soft, its solidity weakened by
the water that has flooded it. And yet it doesn't seem unsafe, as the roots keep
it compact. To the south, the earth becomes firmer and firmer, as high grass
takes the place of the reeds, and you can see a wooden structure floating on the
waters of the river.
name: Among the Reeds

desc:
The remnants of an old loading bay sway gently over the waters. In olden times,
this pier was used to unload goods that came from the northern vales, or even
the valuable loads from the distant Gondor in the south. But those were other
days, and now the quay has fallen into disuse. The wood is starting to rot away,
and a few planks fell off long ago. Some loose threads are all that remains of
the mooring ropes. A small outhouse, once used as storing area, crumbled long
ago into a pile of broken planks. Only the dock itself looks relatively
well-preserved, but even so, it doesn't give you any sort of confidence in its
stability.
name: Abandoned Jetty

desc:
A number of trees grow scattered on this gentle, grassy slope that rises very
slowly towards the east away from the Anduin. Some of them stand lonely, as if
they had been expelled from the very earth by some unknown force, while others
group together in small clusters. The high, fresh grass crowds around their
trunks, as if trying to challenge them, sometimes concealing them by several
feet.
name: Some Dispersed Trees

desc:
The grasslands extend endlessly all around, and, from the distance, they seem to
tinge the ground with a thick layer of intense green dye. However, a few
features catch your eye: some trees grow scattered on the plain to the west, and
there are some to the north too, but they stand together there with a somewhat
dreadful look. In the opposite direction rises a small hillock with soft slopes,
behind which the meadowlands spread.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
Rising slowly over the plains, this soft slope ascends towards the top of a
small hillock to the east, where the old ruins of a wooden house still stand in
a rather precarious condition. If there ever was a track leading up the
hillside, it must have faded long ago, swallowed by the abundant grass that
carpets the ground in deep green. The rear wall of what seems to be a building
stands atop the hillock, a small door leading inside.
name: A Soft Slope to a Ruined Building

desc:
A rickety old large wooden house crowns the top of this low hillock. The walls,
made up of fat logs, are covered in thick moss and lichens, and exude a piercing
smell of moisture, but the fineness of the oaken wood has preserved them from
rotting. The roof seems to have borne worse fate - most of it caved in long ago
- and only the broadest balks stay at their place. In the front wall, the door
has tumbled down inwards, leaving a wide hole through which you can glimpse
numerous broken planks and debris. Over the lintel, a half-rotten wooden sign
seems about to fall off.
name: In Front of a Ruined Tavern

desc:
Over the gentle slope that ascends gradually southwards, the deep green of the
fresh grass mixes with the dark brown of the dug up earth, in small ploughed
patches with deep furrows. The tender shoots of some unrecognizable vegetables
spring up timidly out of the ground in some of them, but others already show
well-grown plants that conceal the dun earth beneath them. The soil is rich in
these lands, and the diverse crops feed their vigorous inhabitants throughout
the year.
name: A Cultivated Hillside

desc:
The tireless grasshoppers seem to have taken possession of this shallow, wet
depression of the ground. Time and time again, they climb up the grass blades to
jump from one shoot into another, often crashing in the air, but only to raise
themselves and start climbing again, in an endless cycle. Sometimes many of them
gather in a small area, and then the swarm appears as a dense mist that boils
with activity.
name: A Hollow in the Grasslands

desc:
Certainly, water must be plentiful in this lands, because no matter what the
weather is like, the stems of the grass are always fresh and wet, and look full
of life. Sometimes, when the sun is shining high in the sky, the little water
drops sliding along their edges mirror the light, adding a diamond-like sparkle
to the deep green colour of the grass, and lightly tinting it with rainbow
coloured reflections.
name: Wet, Grassy Plains

desc:
A large pond has formed on this plain, surrounded by fresh mud soaked by the
cold waters of the Anduin. The stalks of the reeds sprout everywhere, along with
all sort of bushes and weeds that stick out of the mud and the pools. The pond
looks full of life; the background croaking of the frogs and the restless
singing of the crickets mix with the soft sound of the stems grazing in the
wind, only disturbed by the occasional hollow sound of a little beast diving
into the dark water.
name: A Miry Pond

desc:
The ground has become muddy in this mire, and only the filtered water prevents
it from drying. Even so, there are cracks and slits, and even furrow-like splits
running straight as in a ploughed field. The reeds, though not as numerous as in
the marsh to the west, line up along them like small, natural fences, as if
delimiting their own domains. Grey, dense mud fills the widest cracks, forming
small pools that seem to attract vegetation, as it sprouts thronging there.
name: Mudflats

desc:
A group of trees with twisted branches grow in this area of the meadowlands,
like a distant bastion of the dark and shadowy Mirkwood forest miles away to the
east. Their knotted trunks tower above the grass stalks, over which long
branches with dark, sharp-pointed leaves hang. Their dim, almost black tops form
a contrast with the intense green grass on the ground, casting large and
somewhat gloomy shadows upon it.
name: A Cluster of Trees

desc:
In these lands, where water is abundant and grasslands extensive, the soil is
rich in life, and, from the Old Days onward, men have inhabited these dales. As
early as in the First Age, when the Great Enemy whose name shall not be
mentioned had not still been defeated, some tribes of men, that came from the
first Edain, settled in the northern vales. They were known as the Northmen,
although the elves called them Nenedain, and they were related to the men of
Rhovanion and to the ancestors of the Rohirrim. Nowadays, the main inhabitants
of these lands are the Beornings, who protect the vales against the orkish
threat from the mountains.
name: The Fertile Anduin Vales

desc:
Lots of ochre-coloured beehives line up on the flower-dotted grass, and they
impregnate the air with a strong sickly-sweet smell. The Beornings take care of
the bees, and plant flower patches for them. And in exchange, the bees supply
them with the honey they need to bake their honey pies, following the recipe
from their forebears. Some people even affirm that these true-hearted, rude men
can talk to their animals, by using a strange language based on sounds and
gestures, and, judging by their relationship, they may be right.
name: Rows of Beehives

desc:
In the moist soil at the river's edge stands a cluster of weeping willows,
giving the landscape a beautiful, but also a sorrowful and desolate visage. As
the wind rustles the long, thin branches of the trees a strange music is born,
sounding as if the trees were impatient to move. Under the trees there is little
vegetation - all sunlight is absorbed by the willows' hungry leaves. Directly to
the west lies the river Anduin, and to the east, vast grassy plains.
name: Weeping Willows at the River's Edge

desc:
A seemingly ever-present wind rustles the grass of the wide plain, making it
sway and shift in all imaginable nuances of green and yellow. Occasionally, a
small cluster of flowers adds new colours to the landscape, breaking the
monotony. To the east, north and south the vast plains continue seemingly
unending, and to the west lies the great river Anduin. Beyond that, a hazy
bluish grey wall looms - the Misty Mountains.
name: A Grassy Plain

desc:
A great sward of long, golden grass climbs up this low rise amidst the
surrounding landscape of rolling plains. The few silhouettes of the lonely oak
trees or the moving shadow of a distant herd of deer can be seen dotting the
landscape and giving it life. An occasional breeze or gust of wind sweeps down
from the Misty Mountains lying far to the west across the steel-grey surface of
the mighty river Anduin. These open grasslands extend to the horizon in all
other directions, with the ground sloping gradually upwards in the north.
name: A Grassy Hillock

desc:
Green and yellow grass covers this even ground. The air is filled with a heavy
silence, broken with the occasional singing of birds and the whisper of the
wind. Broken blades of grass betray the presence of some animal activity.
name: Grassland

desc:
Amid the low grass grows a patch of colourful flowers. Apparently the flowers
are resilient and appear to bloom all year round - when one wilts, another
springs up. Some are dry already, some are just beginning to sprout.
name: Wild Flowers

desc:
The soil in this fertile valley allows the grass to grow tall and strong. The
unbroken horizon assures that this very landscape will continue for miles and
miles ahead. The sound of water can be heard to the west.
name: High Grass

desc:
As older grass withers and dries up, the new shoots higher and higher.
Entangling with each other, they create a thick curtain hiding the animals and
perhaps the occasional traveller from sight. The grass grows lower to the east,
and to the north a group of stately trees livens up the horizon.
name: High Grass

desc:
A cluster of low, but sturdy trees has settled on the plains. The oaks grow
apart from each other, allowing the sun to reach the lower plants and the
undergrowth. The ground is flat in all directions, and covered with grasses and
herbs.
name: Sparse Oaks

desc:
Lying east of the river Anduin, these grasslands grow in a quiet dignity. The
grass has a lustrous green colour and the land is smooth and gentle. In the
south an outcropping of trees dot the horizon, and in the northeast another
cluster of trees can be seen.
name: Grassland

desc:
A giant tree looms here, towering above the surrounding plains. It seems to be
older than the plains themselves, an ancient oak that has by sheer size survived
the winds and hardships of the plains. The trunk is grizzled and the bark
hardened by many centuries of exposure to the forces of nature, but the top
branches seem young and fresh. At times, the shadow of the tree stretches out
many hundred yards on the plains, that extend in all directions from here. A big
and mossy rock sits here, flat to the ground.
name: Beneath a Big Oak Tree

desc:
In the grass of these fields grow many varieties of flowers, low and high,
adding small touches of colour that stand in sharp contrast with the otherwise
grey, yellow and green of the plains. Overhead, the sky forms a giant vault,
stretching from the eastern horizon to the peaks of the Misty Mountains in the
west. In all directions the plains stretch out, but to the south you can spot a
big tree standing alone.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The grassy fields that roll around and about, are filled with many kinds of
grasses and flowers, making the ground look spotted. When the wind rustles the
grass, these spots swirl in a strange but fascinating pattern. In all directions
the plains stretch out under the great skies above. The ground enters a small
rise to the north, showing more wind-blown grasslands.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The grassy plains here turn from being very flat and low to the north, into a
more rolling and twisting land to the east and south. To the east, a small but
high mound can be spotted, standing out on the otherwise low, rolling plains.
The sky above is a great dome of blue, white and grey, where the clouds play a
constant game chasing each other back and forth. To the south the land reaches a
small ridge, dotted with colourful flowers.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
The land here is absolutely flat. Standing on a small stool, one could probably
see very far, as no ridges or hills obstruct the view. The grass here is of
medium height, neither stretching towards the skies too much, nor hugging the
ground too close, as if it were in some way conscious of its neighbour grass,
not wanting to offend it by standing out in any way. The grasslands stretch out
in every direction.
name: Flat Grasslands

desc:
Here the low, flat ridges that dominate the grasslands to the north seem to have
been ironed out by nature in some strange way, and the land becomes more flat.
Strangely, even the grass seems to have understood this, as no blade seems to
reach higher than its neighbour. To the south the grasslands flatten even more.
name: Grasslands

desc:
From the hill to the north the grasslands spill out again over the plains and
once more resume the shape of the giant, green sea of rustling grass that covers
these lands. The great sky above seems to be larger here than anywhere you have
ever been, completely dominating all life here. To the east, south and west the
grasslands roll on towards a distant horizon.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The carpet of grass that covers these lands makes a small bump here to create a
small grassy hill that, despite being quite low, rises above the surrounding
area. From up here the view is magnificent: the grasslands stretch out in all
directions, and beyond them to the east, a small dark band on the horizon can be
spotted - Mirkwood. To the far, far west a giant grey shape marks the Misty
Mountains.
name: A Small Grassy Hill

desc:
The soft, rolling grasslands lie like a big, green blanket under the great dome
of the sky above, moving and twisting constantly with the wind. As the grass
moves, it displays itself in a great variety of colours - all thinkable nuances
of green, yellow and grey are present, changing all the time. In all directions
this sea of grass extends outwards to the horizon.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The grass here seems higher than that covering the land to the west, the grass
reaches even taller east of here. A deer could be seen in the grass, but smaller
animals would remain completely hidden unless they were stumbled upon or
thoroughly searched for. The grass tips are narrow, but quite tough. Very few
flowers manage to get sunlight in this tall grass.
name: Medium Height Grass

desc:
The healthy grass, as well as the occasional patches of red flowers, sway gently
in the wind, emitting a sweet fragrance. The grasslands continue, seemingly
unchanged in all directions but to the east, where a cluster of trees stand.
name: Grass

desc:
Here the plains seem particularly lively. The grass reflects a deep green
colour, unlike the dusty green that is usual on the steppes. The foliage has
grown tall enough to reach the knees of a man, and small animals are likely to
use it is as shelter. The plains continue in all directions. A patch of flowers
can be seen to the west giving the grassland a slightly different nuance.
name: Lush Grass

desc:
The ground appears to slope a little here, and is soaked with water. Different
kinds of plants thrive here, and all kinds of mud-loving animals. Even though
the place looks very much like a mire, it is firm enough to support the weight
of any animal that may pass by.
name: Wet Meadow

desc:
The ground is soaked with water, forming small, shallow puddles here and there.
The grass grows unhindered, except for the animals grazing on its sweetness.
Meadows spread south, west and north. A whiff of moisture from the east betrays
the presence of a small pond there.
name: Wet Meadow

desc:
This meadow is covered with low, green grass. Many small paths cross it in all
directions, with evident traces of wild life. The northern side is blocked by
the wall the of a building, but all other directions are open and covered with
more grass.
name: Meadow

desc:
Flat and grassy, this stretch of the ground shows signs of use. Here and there a
small circle has been grazed out in the grass. In other places, some low ditches
and barriers have been built out of pressed earth. A house stands to the
northeast and a row of bushes has been planted to block the way north.
name: Grassland

desc:
This vegetation could be the dream for any animal that eats grass - tall, green,
and juicy. A few flowers grow in a cluster but many more seem to have been eaten
and only the stem remains. Apparently there is a water source not very far to
the east since the soil looks even more wet in that direction. Tracks of all
kinds confirm the presence of wild life.
name: Lush Grass

desc:
The ground seems a little wet, and the flowers use this moisture to the outmost.
The grass is very thick, green and juicy. Herbivores would likely satisfy their
hunger on these fields and indeed tracks criss-crossing the fields show sign of
wild life.
name: Lush Grass

desc:
Here the plains are covered with flowers - bluebonnets and poppies. The climate
allows them to bloom during most of the year, creating a colourful carpet on the
face of the steppe. Plants here are thicker and greener than their cousins to
the south and west, probably because they have more moisture and nutrition. The
fields to the north and east seem to sport vegetation just as healthy. A few
stones can be seen, around which different plants have taken root.
name: Blue and Red Flowers

desc:
The character of the grass cover differs from the surrounding fields - the
plants are thicker, greener, and proudly displaying clusters of blue flowers,
bluebonnets. These plants grow in such thick clumps that no ordinary grass can
compete for space in-between them.
name: Bed of Bluebonnets

desc:
The flat, even, grass-covered steppe leads on and on. A few stones lie scattered
about randomly as if giants had thrown them. To the east a slight change in the
colour of the plains suggests different kinds of plants - a welcoming change in
the landscape. A barely visible, and long since dried-up waterbed leads towards
that direction. The field to the north shimmers in a bluish colour and is
seemingly covered with flowers.
name: Grass

desc:
The plains roll out like a great sea of grass under the shifting skies above.
Grasses, herbs and small flowers grow here, rustling and moving in the wind. In
all directions, as far as the eye can see, the plains stretch out, seemingly
endless.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
These grassy plains seem to stretch out forever and appear almost lifeless as
they roll out under the skies. The only detectable movement is the grass that
dances and shifts with the wind, but upon closer inspection small animals seem
to be scurrying in the grass underfoot. The plains stretch out in every
direction.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
These grasslands seem to stretch out forever, the horizon miles away being the
only thing that meets the eye. The tall blades of grass that grow in this
fertile plain, shift and dance in the wind. Flowing like an endless sea, these
waves of grass roll out in all directions from here.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
These flat, grassy plains seem engaged with the wind in a never-ending dance. As
the wind grabs hold of the long blades, they swirl and bend, creating long waves
of grass that roll out over the sea of grass. The plains stretch out in all
directions, with a slope descending west to the thick grassy field.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
The flat, grassy plains lie like a calm, green water beneath the enormous dome
of the sky above. The wind ripples these waters, creating small waves of grass
that seem to follow a hidden and mysterious pattern. In most directions, these
waters stretch out, with the small island of a lonely tree standing in defiance
of the whispering wind. To the west, the ground begins to lower, giving space to
yet another grassy field.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
On these vast, slightly shifting grasslands no shadow falls. The flat lands seem
completely unbroken by hills, heights or trees. The grass that at first seems to
be a monotonous carpet appears, on closer inspection, to sport a variety of
different plants and herbs. It may all look like one big sea, but it consists of
small units of life. A small slope descends to the west while in other
directions the plains stretch further out.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
No height, tree or valley seems to interrupt the vast, flowing grasslands that
cover these plains. The grasses and herbs that grow here seem to forever stretch
out playfully towards the skies, only to be grabbed by the wind and sent into a
merry dance. The grasslands stretch out as far as the eye can see, with a ridge
rising in the east and sloping on to the north.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
Under the great vault of the sky, these endless plains roll out in all
directions, a playing ground where nature's forces put their might to play. The
only thing surviving this game seems to be the tough grass that grows
everywhere. Indeed, it seems to play some strange part in the game, dancing and
creating patterns when moved by the wind.
name: Rolling Plains

desc:
The tall trees that stand here cast long shadows over the flatlands, not making
the plains look less desolate, but rather strengthening the impression of
emptiness. The tall, straight trunks of the beech-trees make them look like
pillars, stretching out for, and supporting, the high vault of the sky above. To
the east stands a great oak-tree in solitude, while to the south the trees stand
more closely together.
name: A Sparsely Forested Plain

desc:
The plains roll out endlessly under the great skies above you. With the great
variety of grass and low herbs, they seem to somehow reflect what is above. As
the wind reaches down and rustles the grass, the lands seem to wave in a strange
dance. The ground descends roughly to the west, reaching out to a riverbank.
name: Rolling Plains

desc:
The tall grass covering these lands seems to shift beneath the skies in a never
ending dance with the wind. The colour of the grass is never constant as it
shifts with weather and rain, being a dark, dull grey when the weather is bad,
and a light, fresh green when blue skies are above. The grasslands stretch out
in all directions.
name: Grasslands

desc:
A shifting mass of grey, green and yellow grass lies all around, matching the
sky that lies above. Vibrant and full with little rushing creatures in the
summertime, dry and almost asleep in the colder months. Broken grass stems here
and there indicate the presence of a bigger beast passing through this area,
perhaps looking for smaller animals to chew on. The grasslands continue in all
directions.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
Rolling out under the skies, these vast grasslands seem to be unending. They are
home to a variety of different grasses, high and low, green and grey, young and
withered. Under the vault of the sky, the grasslands seem to match the heavens
as they stretch out. To the east the ground enters a small rise, offering a bit
higher view over the surrounding land.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
These flat grasslands seem vast and unending as they roll out under the skies.
They sport a variety of different grasses, in all thinkable shades of green and
grey. Some old, withered grasses add to the picture with their yellow, dried
leaves and stems. To the east the land rises towards more open fields. In the
other directions the plains stretch on, flowing like an endless sea.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
Thriving thick and healthy, the grass here grows high towards the sky. Thick
stems and healthy leaves in all shades of green rustle in the passing breezes.
Though quiet, the partly broken and stumped stems confirm the hiding wildlife in
this area. These grasslands continue in every direction while rising in the east
and revealing another endlessly waving plain.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
The tall, swaying grasses that stand here embrace all who enter this deep sea of
green. Looking around is not possible, except over the tallest grass, which
would reach to the shoulder of a grown man. To hide in these grasses would be
easy - just lying down would make one all but invisible. A beast might use such
an opportunity to stalk a traveller of the plains. To the north the ground
rises, bringing more grasslands into the view.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
The grasslands roll out endlessly, low rolling lands covered only with grass
that moves and shifts with the wind. As the grass moves, it shifts in colour,
from a solid green to a pale yellow or dull grey. The skies above seem to
reflect this as clouds come and go in an endless dance. The grasslands lower to
the south into the tall grass.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The low, rolling land is covered with high grass that reaches towards the sky,
only to be grabbed by the wind and sent into a strange dance, creating
mysterious patterns that change constantly. In the stillness, the only thing
heard is the wind and the grass rustling. The plains stretch out in all
directions.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
This small hollow in the ground must have retained some water in the past,
allowing bigger plants to thrive. However, the bushes have dried out since then,
and all that is left are dry roots and sticks entangled with each other. Travel
becomes slightly difficult as the sharp ends of twigs catch both the clothes and
skin.
name: Dry Bushes and Sticks

desc:
A lively patch of grass grows here, between the ruins of an old fire to the
north, stony grounds to the west and dry bushes to the south. However,
underneath the fresh, green grass covering the ground, black residues of old
fire can be recognized. The even plains to the east seem to go on forever.
name: Grass

desc:
The terrain swells a little, forming a very convenient place for a house. Indeed
there are some remains of an unspecified structure here, though almost burned to
the ground. A few charred beams stick up from the ground, wrapped with ivy-like
plants. Seedlings of trees growing among the ruins show that the fire must have
taken place many years ago.
name: Burned Ruins

desc:
The view to the south reveals decaying remains of a homestead. When examining
the ground, it appears to be partly burned and a few scattered trunks still lie
rotten on the ground as in memory of an old fire. Gnarled and black trees cover
the view to the west. Short grass covers the nutritious soil and leads on to the
north. The foliage grows higher to the northeast and east, continuing like that
all the way to the horizon.
name: Grass

desc:
The plains are rolling on and on. The grass tall, but rather small, and yet
nevertheless quite healthy and thick. The grass continues in all directions,
with greener and higher plants to the east, smaller and drier to the west.
name: Short Grass

desc:
An endless grassland extends in all directions, studded with clumps of taller
plants and teeming with life. As the animals are shy and wary, they cannot
always be seen, but the tracks and droppings testify that some animals have
passed here recently. A house, breaking the monotony of the plains, is
noticeable to the northeast.
name: Grassland

desc:
In the midst of these flat grasslands a patch of flowers springs to life. The
stems are thick and green. The flowers, when they can be seen, are small, white
and yellow. Grassland stretch from the southeast to the north. The ground rises
to the northwest.
name: Flowery Patch

desc:
The plants on this stretch of the steppe are in dire need for nutrition: they
look small, dry and withered. The ground is yellowish, and the soil seems to
contain lots of sand. To the south stands a group of small, twisted trees.
Flowers of different colours cover the ground to the north.
name: Short Dry Grass

desc:
The trees here have undergone some unnatural change: they are low, gnarled and
black. Their trunks are scarred, and their lower branches seem to have been
clipped. This effect is most evident to the south. The northern parts of this
coppice appear much healthier. Short grass grows to the north, along with green
crowns of high trees.
name: Gnarled Trees

desc:
Sparsely distributed trees form a small coppice here. The trees have a strange
quality about them: the trunks are black, and all their lower branches are gone.
Black coals lay on the ground, covered however by new foliage.
name: Scorched Trees

desc:
The grass only grows sporadically here, forming small clumps among pebbles and
rocks of different sizes. Since a steep rock wall towers to the west, it is not
difficult to guess the origin of all these stones. On the north, there are some
dark trees, and grasslands extend to the south and east.
name: Scattered Stones

desc:
An immaculate cover of grass extends to the horizon except in the west, where a
darker line may signify a change in the foliage. A careful observer might be
able to spot some small animals around, hurrying in their search for food and
shelter.
name: Grassland

desc:
On these vast grasslands the wind seems to be the only thing moving. But it also
moves the very grass itself, making it dance a strange and unfathomable dance.
Looking closer, one can notice small animals living in the tall grass that
covers these lands. Life is hidden, but it is there. The plains stretch out in
all directions.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The grass ripples when caressed by the wind, making strange patterns appear
everywhere. It resembles a sea, and similarly the life that exists, is seen deep
down and below the surface. Small animals scurry to and from their homes,
feeding their siblings and securing their little lives. The plains continue in
all directions, with an exception of a lowering slope to the south.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
Here the grass stands very tall, reaching a man's chest. It seems to be of
another variety than the grass which covers most of these plains: the stems are
thicker, the blades longer and broader. Hiding in these grasses would be easy
since just lying down would make one all but invisible. The ground rises to the
north, bringing more grasslands into the sight.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
The tall grass continues, coming in from the north. The blades are long and
thick, reaching broadly out of the rich soil. As the wind comes in from the grey
river of Anduin, the grass springs and rustles, bending downwards in the mighty
breeze. Pawsteps of some bigger animal show that a beast of prey is stalking
these lands for its next meal. The grasslands continue in every direction,
rolling out like a giant colourful carpet.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
The plains stretch out here under the open sky as far as the eye can see, the
flat lands covered with high grass that shifts in the wind. Small animals scurry
between the grasses on the ground, almost invisible in the underbrush. As the
wind comes in from the north and west, the grasses shift and dance.
name: Open Plain

desc:
The grasses that cover this open plain are high and strong, their slim,
beautiful blades rustling and dancing in the wind. Below the grasses small
animals live, running as you approach. The grassy plains roll out in all
directions from here, stretching as far as the eye can see.
name: Open Plain

desc:
The plains stretch out endlessly, covered with grass that seems to dance with
the ever-present wind, creating strange and beautiful patterns. In this changing
pattern small animals live, their lives dominated by the search for whatever
food may be found here.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
Here the grasslands rise faintly from west to east, spilling out into the great,
rolling plains that lie between the Great River and Mirkwood. The rise is
covered with low grass, the only vegetation that can survive here on the
windswept rise. To the west flows the mighty Anduin.
name: Rising Grasslands

desc:
The riverbank rises sharply to the east, into the great plains that lie beyond.
The rise is constantly whipped by the winds that come in from the north and
west, over the grey waters of the Anduin, carrying cold moisture with them. The
only thing that grows here is low grass, and even that seems to be on the brink
of survival. To the south a group of small trees can be spotted, swinging their
branches in the breeze.
name: Rising Riverbank

desc:
The gentle slope of the eastern bank of the river is covered in lush grass and
tall stands of cattails swaying in the breeze. The river begins to broaden out
here in small, stagnant pools teeming with life. The marshy ground extends
further to the south, where a large stand of grey willow trees overshadows the
riverbank. Eastwards, the meadows sprawl out over gently rolling hilltops and
broad valleys.
name: At the Bank of the River Anduin

desc:
Here the land rises more steeply to the east, the slopes covered only with small
clusters of grass. The soil is dry and loose here, a result of many years of
slow erosion. The footing is unsafe, making it hard to climb the rise. To the
north the land ascends less steeply, while to the east the grasslands stretch
out beyond the rise.
name: A Small, Grassy Rise

desc:
This small, grassy meadow lies sheltered by low rises that ring this shallow
dell, untouched by the relentless winds. As a result, the land is covered with
small trees, lush rose bushes and herbs of all kinds. To the east the grasslands
continue, while to the west lies the riverbed of the mighty Anduin.
name: A Grassy Meadow

desc:
The grasslands begin here beyond the eastern bank of the river Anduin,
stretching on to the east. The slopes are covered by tall grasses that shift as
the wind comes in from the north and west, carrying with it a faint scent of
water. To the west, a stony slope leads to the top of a small rise by the
Anduin.
name: Rising Grasslands

desc:
Here the land rises from west to east, an extension of the riverbank of the
Anduin. The rise is covered by a variety of grasses that shift in the wind,
depicting at every time a new, unique pattern. Looking towards north, the
grasslands stretch out and another open plain enters the view to the east.
name: Rising Grasslands

desc:
The wind whistles as it passes over these low, grassy lands, playing upon the
grass as if it were an instrument. The sound created may not be called music,
yet it is fitting for these lands in a way. Under the great vault of the sky the
plains stretch out in all directions.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The plains roll out under the great skies, covered with grass that dances in the
wind, seeming almost a reflection of the skies. The colour of the grass shifts
with that of the sky, being a beautiful green when the sky is blue, and turning
a dull grey when the skies do. The plain stretches away from here in all
directions.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
These low, rolling plains are covered with short grass that seems to shimmer as
the wind grabs the blades, joining in a never ending dance. Here and there,
ancient rocks lie about, smoothed over time by the caress of the wind. In all
directions the plains stretch out, and in the distant west you can spot the
great Anduin.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
Silver blades of a foreign variety of grass grow tall on this rolling field.
Light striking the blades causes the whole field to somewhat shimmer and dance
in an almost magical fashion. The plains continue in all directions. Further to
the west, a small grassy hillock can be spotted, rising in the plains.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The ground evens out here; not even the slightest swelling can be seen. The
grass changes its colour in different spots: brownish here, reddish there and
yellowish at yet another part of the flat plain. A dark shape breaks the
straight line of the northern horizon.
name: Flat and Grassy Terrain

desc:
A massive rock rises from the surface of the surrounding grassland. It stands in
solitude among the seemingly endless plains. Small cracks have been carved into
the rock, looking somewhat like a natural stair. The grassy plains continue
rather unchanged in all directions. A few stones can be seen scattered to the
east.
name: At a Massive Rock

desc:
Open plains covered with grass - such is the landscape here. As far as one can
see, the same kind of environment stretches all the way from southwest to north.
Among the grass to the south, a huge lonely rock can be spotted. Dark, scattered
trees grow to the east.
name: Grass

desc:
The grass is low and weak, very distinct from the lush plains to the southwest.
The northern parts are visibly sloping down, and are even more scattered,
covered just with small clumps of grasses amidst pebbles and gravel. Low, dark
line of trees meets the eye looking to the east.
name: Grass

desc:
The ground forms a slight depression here. It is filled with sand, gravel and
pebbles. It is not quite a desert, plants are still growing here. It is just
that the grass is sparse, low and delicate with long stretches of sandy ground
in between.
name: Sandy Depression

desc:
The rocks and pebbles covering the ground hinder the growth of the grass. The
area is sparsely covered with low, spiny bushes that are almost devoid of leaves
and flowers. Their twigs are mostly dried and sharp, making it easy to prick
one's skin here. To the south is a patch of smaller gravel and sand. To the
north looms a low, dark ridge across the plains.
name: Dried Twigs and Pebbles

desc:
Golden grass grows high on this vast plain. Animal tracks lay scattered about
the terrain, leaving signs of movement onto the grass. Although a dandelion or
two bloom in the thick grass, nothing else grows here. To the north a tall stand
of trees can be seen towering towards the sky.
name: South of a Tall Outcrop

desc:
There is a group of oak trees to the west, easily detected on the flat horizon
created by these grassy plains. Delicate flowers peek through the bold grass,
which is thick and strong. A cluster of what looks like dandelions can be
spotted to the south.
name: Grass

desc:
Amid the grasses, another plant has won a piece of land. The seeds must have
floated in on the wind and taken root. Now the whole area is covered with
dandelions - yellow in spring, white in the fall, but green all year round.
name: Dandelions

desc:
Deer tracks cover the ground, as well as other signs of animal life. The grass
grows thick and tall, providing enough coverage for a large animal to hide in
it. A large rock, rising high above the rather flat plains, is seen to the
southeast. The plains extend in all directions and the grass grows exceptionally
high to the west and northwest.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
Grass grows thick and green here, leaving little room for anything else. It
bends slightly as you move through it. Eastward an outcrop of rock can be seen,
but in other directions smooth flow of grasslands are all that exists.
name: Grass

desc:
The steppe-like terrain continues, covered with grass and a few rickety bushes.
The undulating ground bulges here and there, but the terrain remains dirty-green
in all directions. Tracks of animals of different sizes lay scattered about the
terrain.
name: Grassy Terrain

desc:
Here the grasslands begin, stretching out to the east. The plains are covered
with tall grass that seems to dance with the gusts of wind. Sweeping over the
plains from time to time, the breezes fill the silence with the rustling of
grass, and at the same time emphasizing that very silence. The only part of the
landscape that intrudes upon this is the occasional cry of a lone bird high
above the plains.
name: Open Grasslands

desc:
The grasslands stretch out as far as the eye can see to the east. Here they
cover small rises and hills that have long since been worn down, the once sharp
rocks softened and dulled by the roots of small plants. Here one may find small
pockets shielded from the ever-present wind. Small, twisted trees and bushes
stand on these, forever opposing the environment in which they live.
name: Rolling Meadowlands

desc:
Here, shielded from the wind by the small hills to the north and the willows to
the west, a small field is covered by vibrant wildflowers. In an otherwise
unfriendly environment they manage to flourish, adding a welcome touch of colour
to the otherwise bleak landscape dominated by shades of green, yellow and grey.
To the west lies the Anduin, its eastern bank lined with willows, and to the
east the grasslands stretch out, seemingly endless.
name: A Field of Wildflowers

desc:
Amidst the lush reeds and grasses that flourish here, a stand of great hoary
willow trees line the soft bank of the Anduin. The long and slender tips of
narrow leaves fluttering in the breeze hang down, nearly touching the water. The
flat, blue-grey surface of the river extends far out westward, unbroken in its
breadth. Beyond the river, grassy plains quickly tumble into broken foothills
and then rise, soaring far above the plain in snow-capped peaks. Gentle
grasslands roll out as far as the eye can see towards the eastern horizon.
name: A Willow Stand at the Bank of the Anduin

desc:
Here the soil is too rocky to support any trees. Even the hard willows cannot
find enough soil to root themselves. The only vegetation consists of a few
flowers and some low bushes. The wind rushes in from the northwest, carrying
with it a scent of water and cool moisture. To the east the grasslands begin to
descend slightly, stretching out as far as the eye can see.
name: The East Bank of the River Anduin

desc:
Here the bank of the river rises slightly above the grey-blue surface of the
waters. On this rise, large boulders can be seen strewn in what almost resembles
a pattern of sorts. Maybe these shores were once someone's home, or perhaps
nature yet again plays us a trick. In the skies above, changes take place as
